newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sugar mill investors suing Nicaraguan gov't.
newsitem.headline: Sugar mill investors suing Nicaraguan gov't.

text.p: British, Swiss and Nicaraguan investors said on Wednesday they will sue the Nicaraguan government for trying to backtrack in the privatization of a key sugar mill.
"We are going to sue the government for this outrage," president of the Victoria de Julio mill's owners, Edgard Chamorro said at a news conference.
Last week Nicaragua's Attorney General's Office asked a judge to annul the 1993 privatization of the country's largest sugar mill.

The government of President Arnoldo Aleman has said former President Violeta Chamorro sold the mill at about $4.5 million instead of its value of more than $220 million, to Agroindustrial Azucarera (Agroinsa), a private consortium of Sandinista industrialists.
Stockholders of the mill deny the claim, and say they bought the mill for $20 million in a public auction.
Agroinsa's Chamorro sided with interested investors at the Cuban-built sugar mill, who asked the government to reconsider its decision.

"The message we are getting is that we should look in other countries that offer greater investor security," Nicaraguan representative of British commodities group E.D.&F. Man Plc Louis Anthony Martin said.
The British firm bought a 30 percent stake in the mill in January, Martin said, "confiding in investor rhetoric."
